candidates.title: `ContentManager.cpp`'s Windows video guard is wrong on native MSVC
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-051 — `ContentManager.cpp`'s Windows video guard is wrong on native MSVC
**Severity: medium · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: `modules/content`, `modules/media`**

`modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp:47` guards the `Video.hpp` include with
`#if !defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__) && !defined(__ANDROID__) && !defined(__MINGW32__) && !defined(__MINGW32__)`
— `__MINGW32__` is checked twice and plain `_WIN32`/native MSVC is not checked at all, while the
CMake condition that actually excludes the video sources is
`if(MINGW OR WIN32 OR EMSCRIPTEN OR ANDROID)` (`modules/CMakeLists.txt:15-19`). On a native MSVC
Windows build the header include survives while `modules/media/src/Xna/Video/{Video,VideoPlayer}.cpp`
are excluded from the build — a link error. The project's own D3D11/D3D12 CI targets exactly this
configuration.

candidates.title: `SongTypeReader` advertises three extensions this build cannot decode
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-052 — `SongTypeReader` advertises three extensions this build cannot decode
**Severity: low · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: `modules/content`, `modules/media`**

`LooseFileContentTypeReader<Media::Song>::Extensions()` returns
`{".mp3", ".ogg", ".wav", ".flac", ".opus", ".aac", ".wma"}`
(`modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp:2996-3001`). CNA's vendored SDL3_mixer build
explicitly disables Opus, WavPack, mpg123 and libFLAC-alternative decoders
(`cmake/ThirdPartySDL.cmake:149-160`); `.opus`, `.aac` and `.wma` have no decoder in this
configuration. `Content.Load<Song>()` on such a file will fail at the point of actual decode, not
at resolution.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: Song advertises seven extensions; support remains decoder/build dependent and not queried during resolution

candidates.summary: AudioMixer::DestroyMixer (SDL3 mixer) has no production caller: the generation counter and reload machinery protect a teardown that occurs only in tests and tools/audio harnesses. As read, at exit the device is closed by the static g_audioDevice's destructor and the native mixer pointer is never destroyed, unlike the immortal ALSA engine with its atexit close.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: SoundEffectInstance::Play calls CNA::Internal::Audio::EnsureMixer() directly, so a mixer-creation failure at that point would surface as std::runtime_error rather than NoAudioHardwareException (the effect constructor normally creates the mixer first, so this is reachable only if creation fails later, e.g. after a mixer teardown).
candidates.note: by reading; not executed

candidates.summary: Under CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=ALSA the SoundEffect, SoundEffectInstance, DynamicSoundEffectInstance, Cue, SoundBank, WaveBank and offline-renderer suites are filtered out of CnaTests (they read SDL3_mixer track handles); XNA-facade coverage on ALSA rests on CnaMixerXnaTests, CnaMixerTests, AudioCategoryTests and the microphone suites.
candidates.note: coverage limit rather than a defect

candidates.summary: Stale comments: SoundEffect.cpp says FireAndForgetPanState is freed in OnFireAndForgetStopped (code defers it to the next Play/exit); SoundEffect.hpp documents SoundEffect::Play as returning false 'if the instance limit was reached' although the implementation checks no limit; SoundEffectInstance.hpp says is3D_ never resets although Pan before the first Play resets it; the content SoundEffectContentTypeReader.hpp describes a synthetic-WAV FromStream route while the .cpp constructs via the raw-buffer constructor.
candidates.note: documentation-comment drift; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: FNA_KEYBOARD_USE_SCANCODES is honoured only by the legacy bridge and Keyboard::GetKeyFromScancodeEXT; no platform keyboard service consults it, so Keyboard::GetState is not layout-independent under it, while docs/platform-input-notes.md still describes scancode mode as layout-independent polling.
candidates.note: by reading; not executed; recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Comments in Sdl3Platform.cpp and X11Platform.cpp (and plans/plan_platform.md) refer to Game::UpdateInput(), which does not exist; the pump is the tail of Game::PollEvents.
candidates.note: stale comment; cosmetic

candidates.summary: Game::PollEvents' F9/F10 renderer debug hooks have no build guard, so every game build reserves those keys for the renderer's context-loss seam (a no-op except in renderer families that override it).
candidates.note: design limit rather than a defect; the frame page records the same fact

candidates.summary: Wheel granularity differs between backends: SDL3 snapshots discard sub-notch motion, the Win32 snapshot accumulates raw WHEEL_DELTA units.
candidates.note: parity difference; not shown to be wrong against XNA

candidates.summary: InputManager::SetMouseRelativeMode has no non-test caller, so the legacy accumulator's relative-delta path never accumulates in production.
candidates.evidence: modules/input/src/Internal/InputManager.cpp; call-site search of modules excluding tests
candidates.note: cosmetic; retained for legacy bridge tests

candidates.summary: docs/input-backend.md says SdlInputBridge retains a raw ProcessEvent overload for legacy SDL-shaped tests and cites src/Input/Internal/InputManager.cpp; at this snapshot SdlInputBridge.hpp declares no ProcessEvent and the file is src/Internal/InputManager.cpp.
candidates.note: in-repo documentation drift

candidates.summary: MediaPlayer::Play(Song*) clears the queue and then reads the given Song. If the caller passes a Song owned by the queue (for example the active song), Clear() has already destroyed it, so LoadSong reads a destroyed object. Source-read; not executed; no test found.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Play(Song*) compares the old queue's first song (a copy) with the caller's pointer to decide whether to flag ActiveSongChanged, so for library or standalone songs the flag is raised on every call, including replaying the same song.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Play(const SongCollection&, index) does not set the ActiveSongChanged dispatcher flag (only the state-change flag, via PlaySong), whereas Play(Song*), NextSong and the end-of-queue path do.
candidates.evidence: modules/media/src/Xna/MediaPlayer.cpp (Play(const SongCollection&, index), Play(Song*), NextSong, Update)
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Play(Song*) passes the caller's Song to PlaySong, so the mixer duration and play count land on the library's Song, and Stop() only resets play counts on queue copies; comments in MediaLibrary.cpp still say MediaPlayer::Play operates on a duplicate and never backfills library songs.
candidates.note: documentation/comment drift plus behaviour to characterise; recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: A failed PlaySong (load, track creation, attach or start failure) returns before the timer and state are touched. If the player was already Playing, the old track has been destroyed but the state stays Playing with no track and no ended flag, so Update never advances. Source-read; not executed.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: MediaPlayer::ProgramExit is documented as called at application exit but has no runtime call site; within modules only the C API route cna_media_player_program_exit_ext calls it.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: A Song copy that fails to construct (file removed after the scan) throws FileNotFoundException out of Play after the queue was already cleared and possibly partly filled.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Without a mixer (SDL2 or NULL audio) queue copies never receive a duration and DetectSongEndedByElapsedTime ignores zero durations, so songs never auto-advance in that profile.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: VideoPlayer keeps a raw Video* and Video keeps a raw VideoPlayer* parent; CloseDecoder writes through the stored Video*, so destroying a Video before its player is stopped, disposed or destroyed would write through a dangling pointer. The header states no lifetime rule. Source-read; not executed.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: VideoPlayer::GetTexture does not catch exceptions from the decoder (std::runtime_error for decode, resample and I/O errors), and the header documents only ObjectDisposedException for it.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: MediaLibraryIndex.hpp's class comment lists four scanned extensions while the implementation also indexes .flac and .opus.
candidates.note: comment drift, not a code defect

candidates.summary: No test found for: the natural song-end path under SDL3_mixer, the no-mixer or failed-install visualization branch, MediaLibrary::Dispose semantics, or a throwing path in SavePicture beyond the sanitizer cases.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: A genuine switch to a different video stream does not seek the demuxer or flush, so the new codec context starts at the current position; no fixture has a second video stream and only the same-stream no-op and out-of-range cases are tested.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: The pixel-conversion path applies one BT.601 integer matrix without range expansion or a BT.709 branch to all planar formats, including YUVJ; colour checks are +/-20 tolerance on one frame of synthetic bars.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: The FFmpeg probe states no minimum version while the sources rely on the FFmpeg 5.1-era channel-layout API, so an older pkg-config-visible FFmpeg would likely fail at compile time instead of configure time (not tried).
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: Trailing truncation of a Matroska file is reported as a clean end of stream rather than an error, so a truncated file plays to the point of truncation without any exception.
candidates.note: characterised behaviour, not a defect; recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue
